key_insight: A D-gun applied Al2O3-TiO2 ceramic coating markedly improves the wear resistance of Ti-6Al-4V, and the wear response can be predicted effectively with machine learning.
engineering_relevance: This work shows a practical route to extend the service life of titanium alloy components in aerospace, biomedical, and marine tribological environments.
method: Applied ~200 µm Al2O3-TiO2 coating on Ti-6Al-4V using detonation gun spraying.
Evaluated wear using ASTM G99 pin-on-disc tests at 40–100 N, 100–200 rpm, and 20–40 min against EN31 steel.
Trained ANN, KNN, and random forest models to predict wear from sliding parameters.
evidence_signal: The coated samples showed reduced wear and tribo-layer formation, and random forest gave the lowest mean percentage error and mean squared error among the tested models.
watch_item: The reported ML performance is based on a limited experimental parameter range, so broader validation is needed before generalizing to other loads, speeds, or coating conditions.
paper_title: Tribological enhancement of Al 2 O 3 -TiO 2 D-gun coated Ti-6Al-4V alloy: A machine learning approach
